record.context_brief: Local substitutions for weighted perfect-matchings enumeration
record.original_question: In weighted graph enumeration of perfect matchings, characterize the local graph substitutions that change the weighted sum of matchings by a predictable factor or preserve it exactly.

evidence.quote: One then looks at local substitutions with a graph that preserve the sum of the weights of the matchings, or more generally, multiply the sum of the weights of the matchings by some predictable factor.
Problem 17: Characterize those local substitutions that have a predictable effect on the weighted sum of matchings of a graph.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G = (V, E, w)$ be a finite edge-weighted graph, with weight function $w: E \to R$ taking values in a commutative ring $R$. Define the matching generating polynomial (weighted perfect-matching sum) of $G$ by
$$M(G) \;=\; \sum_{\mu} \prod_{e \in \mu} w(e),$$
where the sum is over all perfect matchings $\mu$ of $G$. A local substitution rule is a pair $(H_1, H_2)$ of finite edge-weighted graphs each carrying a distinguished set of boundary vertices, together with a procedure that, given any graph $G$ containing an embedded copy of $H_1$ (matched to the boundary), produces a new graph $G'$ by removing the interior of $H_1$ and gluing in $H_2$ along the same boundary vertices. The substitution is said to have a predictable effect on weighted matchings if there exists a function $\Phi$ (depending only on $H_1, H_2$ and the boundary data, not on the rest of $G$) such that for every host graph $G$,
$$M(G') \;=\; \Phi \cdot M(G).$$
The constant case $\Phi \equiv 1$ corresponds to local substitutions that preserve the weighted sum of perfect matchings exactly. Examples of such substitutions include the "urban renewal" (spider) move and various vertex- and edge-splitting moves.

Problem: Characterize all local graph substitutions $(H_1, H_2)$ that have a predictable effect on the weighted sum of perfect matchings, i.e., that multiply $M(G)$ by a factor depending only on the local data $(H_1, H_2)$ and its boundary, independently of the ambient graph $G$. In particular, give a complete description (e.g., algebraic or combinatorial classification) of those substitutions that exactly preserve $M(G)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears as Problem 17 in Propp's survey "Enumeration of Matchings: Problems and Progress." While many specific local substitutions (urban renewal/spider move, vertex splitting, edge contractions, graphical condensation moves, and chip-removal / Pfaffian-preserving moves) have been identified and used extensively in the literature, no complete characterization of all predictable local substitutions appears to be known. Subsequent work (e.g., on the octahedron recurrence, generalized urban renewal, and graphical condensation) extends the catalogue of such moves but does not provide a full classification.

status_evidence.title: Enumeration of Matchings: Problems and Progress
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 17: Characterize those local substitutions that have a predictable effect on the weighted sum of matchings of a graph.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open problem in Propp's survey, with only specific examples (such as urban renewal) known.

status_evidence.title: Perfect Matchings and The Octahedron Recurrence
status_evidence.snippet: Generalizations of urban renewal and graphical condensation moves on edge-weighted graphs are studied.
status_evidence.claim: Further families of predictable local substitutions have been introduced, but no complete characterization is given.

status_evidence.title: Calculation of Pfaffians by a Chip Removal
status_evidence.snippet: Local chip-removal moves are described that have predictable effects on Pfaffians and hence on weighted matching sums.
status_evidence.claim: Additional examples of such moves continue to be discovered, indicating the classification problem remains open.
